description: An emulation of tape worn out by age and use: noise, a loss of treble and a loss of level, all drifting as the tape runs

params.text: Sets how worn the tape is: it adds noise and takes up to 24dB off the level
Sets how old the tape is, sweeping the treble loss from 20000Hz down to 200Hz and bringing in more noise as it rises
Sets how much the treble loss and the level wander about their settings as the tape runs; at the left they hold to what the knobs say
Shapes the noise by the level of the signal, so the hiss follows what is playing instead of running underneath it, and lengthens the level detector's release as it rises

notes: all four knobs come up fully anticlockwise, which is no noise, no level loss and no treble loss, so a new module passes the audio through unchanged.
the noise is only shaped by the signal while the envelope knob is off its lowest setting; at zero the noise runs at a steady level.
the module has no menu of its own beyond Rack's.
